note: Plain-language grouping of the 23 COLE tasks for the mockups. The live site groups them in 9 groups; here they are merged into 7. Keys are the normalized task keys of the leaderboard (see normalizeBenchmarkName in COLE/frontend/src/app/leaderboard/util.js).

plain.en: Does the model tell a happy review from an angry one?
plain.fr: Le modèle distingue-t-il un avis content d'un avis fâché ?

plain.en: Given one sentence, does another one follow, contradict it or say something unrelated?
plain.fr: Une phrase en entraîne-t-elle une autre, la contredit-elle ou n'a-t-elle aucun lien ?

plain.en: Can it find the answer in a passage, or say yes or no to a question?
plain.fr: Trouve-t-il la réponse dans un texte, ou répond-il par oui ou non à une question ?

plain.en: Can it spot the sentence that is written correctly?

label.fr: Sens des mots et des phrases

plain.en: Does it see that two sentences say the same thing, and which sense of a word is meant?
plain.fr: Voit-il que deux phrases disent la même chose, et quel sens d'un mot est visé ?

plain.en: Can it work out which person or thing a pronoun points to?
plain.fr: Sait-il à quelle personne ou chose renvoie un pronom ?

plain.en: Does it know Quebec expressions and words?
plain.fr: Connaît-il les expressions et les mots du Québec ?

excluded_keys.frblimp: Present in all 96 snapshot entries but absent from the site's benchmark list, and its value equals qfrblimp in every entry (checked on the snapshot). Treated as a duplicate of qfrblimp and left out of the 23 tasks. The live site's overall score still counts it, so overall_site in models.json keeps the site formula.

uncertain_tasks.reason: The live benchmarks page files it under 'Paraphrase detection', but its title (Quebec-French linguistic minimal pairs) and the sibling multiblimp say it is a grammar task; its English description on the site reads like a paraphrase task (copy of PAWS). Placed in grammar. To confirm with the authors.
Relatedness and entailment on sentence pairs; the site files it under natural language inference. Kept in reasoning, though its Pearson metric is a similarity score.
Paraphrase detection: kept with meaning (sts22, wsd) rather than reasoning.

Its exact_match values are below 1 in the data (for example 0.03), so the site rule 'values above 1 are divided by 100' leaves them as fractions; if they are really percentages the score is 100 times too high. Rule kept as the site applies it; to verify.
